# Catalogue review — 2 October 2026

The supplied 300-entry list adds 256 field stops to the existing 33, giving 289 distinct destinations. Six entries are included under their parent building and five are excluded below. All names on the website are English.

## Model and photograph coverage

275 destinations have a model: the 33 existing detailed studies and 242 additions with mapped OSM massing. 14 destinations currently use location markers. 272 destinations have a credited photograph. These are not 289 detailed reconstructions.

Central London retains its continuous 3D surroundings. Distant destinations use local context patches, without loading all of Greater London. Photos load when their card is opened. Buildings without a verified facade study still support browser-local visit records; they do not claim to reveal realistic exterior finishes.

## Excluded entries

- #57 **Smith Square Georgian Terraces** — A general group of Georgian terraces without specified addresses; St John's Smith Square remains included.
- #195 **Robin Hood Gardens (former site)** — Demolished estate (2017–2025); not represented as an extant building.
- #221 **Shad Thames Warehouses** — Broad warehouse district; Butler's Wharf is retained as a specific destination.
- #224 **Bermondsey Spa Regeneration Area** — An unspecified group of regeneration schemes, without individual building names or boundaries.
- #252 **One Tree Hill Community Centre** — No identifiable London building could be verified under this exact name. A precise address or reference is needed.

Robin Hood Gardens demolition reference: [Victoria and Albert Museum](https://www.vam.ac.uk/event/3lzLmPwXdG/focus-on-robin-hood-gardens-july-2025). One Tree Hill Community Centre can be revisited if a precise address or authoritative reference is supplied.

## Corrections and scope

- Emery Walker’s House is **7 Hammersmith Terrace**, corrected from 8 in the input. [Official address](https://www.emerywalker.org.uk/visit).
- The former Jewish Museum on Albert Street is retained as a building, with its former use made explicit.
- The historic Royal London Hospital is represented by the former building, now Tower Hamlets Town Hall, rather than the newer hospital tower.
- The two UCL East buildings, two RCA campuses and three Kew glasshouses are separate stops.
- Large complexes are represented by their mapped buildings. This may include later additions; the model is not a reconstruction of a single historical period.

## Location-only stops

- #10 **Christ Church Greyfriars Ruins** — Ruined church and garden; surviving fragments are not yet separately modelled.
- #11 **Watts Memorial, Postman’s Park** — A memorial shelter and tiled wall, not a conventional building volume.
- #18 **Panorama St Paul’s** — The source footprint is still tagged as construction. A model of the completed retrofit has not yet been verified.
- #37 **St Dunstan in the East** — Church ruins and garden; surviving fragments are not yet separately modelled.
- #53 **Westminster Underground Station** — Underground station. Subsurface spaces are not modelled.
- #124 **Maiden Lane Estate** — The estate location is included, with mapped buildings in its surroundings. An exact selection of its original blocks has not yet been verified.
- #130 **Highpoint II** — The available OSM selection overlaps Highpoint I. Highpoint II is kept as a separate field stop, without a duplicated or invented mass.
- #143 **Penguin Pool, London Zoo** — Lubetkin’s Penguin Pool: the pool and ramps need a dedicated model.
- #144 **Snowdon Aviary, London Zoo** — A lightweight aviary structure; mesh and cable geometry need a dedicated model.
- #198 **Canary Wharf Underground Station** — Underground station. Subsurface spaces are not modelled.
- #209 **Former Waterloo International Terminal** — The source mass is included under Waterloo Station. The former international terminal is retained as a distinct field stop; its roof has not yet been separated.
- #253 **Walter’s Way** — The self-build street is located, but individual house footprints are missing from the source snapshot. No substitute boxes have been added.
- #254 **Segal Close** — The self-build street is located from its address area, but individual house footprints are missing from the source snapshot. No substitute boxes have been added.
- #297 **Alton Estate** — The estate is represented by surrounding mapped buildings; an exact estate-wide model selection is not yet defined.

## Geometry and reuse

OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL 1.0. Cached Greater London extract: 29 September 2026, with the previous central-London geometry preserved. Source links are on each card. Coordinates share the original AEQD metre origin (51.51° N, 0.106° W). Recorded height, storey estimates and 12 m assumptions remain distinct. No random infill or bounding-box building replacements are used. New massing does not imply surveyed height, roof geometry or facade detail.

Individual model downloads use Rhino 6 mesh format and can be opened in Rhino 7. Keep each supplied local origin for reimport. Regional files use the shared city origin.
